summary.name: Digital media
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing digital media: media content encoded in machine-readable digital formats, its history, its impact on industries and society, and related copyright issues.
use_cases: Researching history of digital media and computing
Learning about marketing media categories (paid, owned, earned)
Studying copyright issues for online content
Background reading on digital transformation of industries
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines digital media as digitized text, audio, video and graphics delivered through screens or speakers, and gives examples such as software, web pages, MP3 audio and e-books. It traces history from Babbage and Ada Lovelace through Vannevar Bush's 1945 "As We May Think" essay to the digital computer and mobile phone era. It also covers the effects of digital media on journalism, publishing, entertainment and education, plus copyright, fair use and open licensing.
notable: Covers history from Babbage and Lovelace to the digital revolution
Explains paid, owned and earned media categories
Discusses copyright, fair use and open content licensing
caveats: Not a software tool; it is an informational article
Some statistics are dated (e.g., 2014 to 2020 projections) and several claims lack citations
